thread.title: Apple planning big SoCal expansions in San Diego and Culver City

author: Ben Miller
title: Apple planning big SoCal expansions in San Diego and Culver City
text: – Contributing Writer, L.A. Biz Dec 13, 2018, 7:05am PST Apple Inc. said it's planning big expansions in San Diego and Culver City in Southern California. Early this morning, Cuppertino, California-based Apple (Nasdaq: AAPL) said it would invest $1 billion in a new campus in north Austin, Texas. The company also said it plans to establish new sites in Seattle, San Diego and Culver City and expand in Pittsburgh, New York and Boulder, Colorado over the next three years. Apple said that over the next three years, it will expand to more than 1,000 employees in Seattle, San Diego and Culver City each. “Talent, creativity and tomorrow’s breakthrough ideas aren’t limited by region or zip code, and, with this new expansion, we’re redoubling our commitment to cultivating the high-tech sector and workforce nationwide," said Tim Cook , Apple CEO, in a statement announcing the expansion. Apple currently employs 6,200 people in Austin and with the plans to build a new complex there, one mile away from the current location, "the 133-acre campus will initially accommodate 5,000 additional employees, with the capacity to grow to 15,000, and is expected to make Apple the largest private employer in Austin," Apple said. The Austin location is Apple's second-largest employment hub, trailing only Cuppertino. In California, Apple said it currently employs more than 36,000 people. There are 53 Apple retail stores in the state and nearly 4,000 suppliers. "California has the highest concentration of Apple suppliers and app economy jobs of any state," according to the company. According to Apple, it "added 6,000 jobs to its American workforce in 2018 and now employs 90,000 people in all 50 states." “Apple is proud to bring new investment, jobs and opportunity to cities across the United States," Cook said, adding that Apple recently opened its newest office in Nashville, Tennessee and Apple’s Miami office is projected to double in size.
